summary: Deny-by-default, custom-claim authority and participant/owner checks are strong. Confirmed MapDiff addition/removal bypasses and the replayable client promo counter update are fixed and covered. Legacy schema breadth and the recursive support-admin read fallback retain minor hardening gaps.

findings.issue: Conversation read-marker and promo update validators previously used changedKeys(), which ignored additions and removals. Emulator reproductions confirmed the bypasses.
findings.recommendation: Completed locally: affectedKeys() now guards both document and nested-map diffs, with deny regressions.

findings.issue: Several legacy self-owned user/review/learning-data writes do not apply one complete schema validator with size limits to every field.
findings.recommendation: Harden one domain at a time with emulator characterization; do not introduce a broad schema rewrite in this maintenance slice.

findings.issue: The recursive custom-claim admin read fallback exposes new unmatched operational roots to support admins unless they are added to the protected list.
findings.recommendation: The manifest and regression test make the behavior explicit. Review every new root and prefer explicit admin reads for sensitive domains.

attack_attempts.outcome: Private collections reject unauthenticated scans. packages and avatars are documented public exceptions; events_public requires authentication and active status.
Dedicated suites deny cross-user access for users, sessions, trial, transactions, conversations, events and provider internals.
Emulator reproduced conversation and promo field addition/removal bypasses; affectedKeys() fixes and deny regressions now pass.
Client-creatable user, review, message and teacher-request paths bind identity to auth UID/path/ref. Server-only domains deny client create.
Authority fields are immutable or server-owned in validated domains; conversation marker updates now affect only the caller key.
Event, teacher-request, caption and conversation validators protect immutable fields. Some legacy owner-only documents have no explicit schema; see finding.
Sensitive event, caption, teacher-request and navigation writes have type checks. Legacy self-owned learning data remains only identity-scoped.
Client create is denied for most lifecycle domains. Conversation/promo MapDiff mismatch is fixed; legacy owner schemas remain a follow-up.
Captions, event text, event chat and teacher evidence are bounded. Several legacy user/review/learning fields lack complete size limits.
Strict validators enforce required fields in event, caption, chat and teacher-request creates. Legacy owner-only collections are not fully validated.
Admin authority comes only from Firebase Auth custom claims; user documents cannot assign admin. Teacher and server-owned fields have deny regressions.
Strict domains use hasOnly/hasAll and the confirmed MapDiff bypass is fixed. Legacy user/review/learning documents remain a bounded follow-up.
Call, trial, billing, membership and moderation lifecycle writes are server-only. Direct event edit remains active-to-active.
Teacher proof paths are scoped to users/<auth uid>/teacherVerification/proofs/<file>. Identity refs in chat/reviews are exact.
Client-created chat/caption/teacher data and direct event edits use request.time or immutable timestamps where state depends on them.
Event capacity, rating and caption confidence/utterance values are range-checked. Legacy owner numeric fields remain schema candidates.
users reads are owner/admin scoped; userPublicProfiles is a separate signed-in projection. Tests reject cross-user private reads.
Direct client promo writes are denied; the callable transaction creates the per-user redemption and increments usageCount through Admin SDK.
Conversation messages and event participant/chat reads validate parent state. Owner-scoped users subcollections cannot cross UID boundaries.
Suites cover users uid, participantMap inbox, active events/participants and bounded chat queries. Dart verifies event indexes; emulator does not prove deployment.
Sensitive updates call domain validators or are server-only. Some owner-only learning/review writes lack complete schema validators.
